headline.production: Production is still dead: both old Railway addresses answer Railway's own 404. Eleven phases are merged on GitHub (P1, P2a, P3a, P6a, P7a, P8a, P9-0a, P12a, P12, L2, L4); none is deployed, because nothing reaches a server or a phone before your pre-flight.
headline.critical: Your pre-flight (P0a) has not started. It is the critical path: nothing reaches a phone or a server until it is done. Its first two answers are already needed: the domain name you will use, and the highest app version number on any technician's phone. The drain tooling is built and reviewed and waits only for those two. New on 2026-11-14: GitHub has stopped running the automatic checks (billing: the month's included minutes are used up or a payment failed), and on 2026-11-14 you allowed merging on this PC's own runs of the same checks meanwhile, so merges continue. Restoring GitHub's checks is still worth doing when you can. I used far more of those minutes than I should have: every note I saved to the plan started a full run. That is stopped. On 2026-11-14 you started the web defects phase (the drain needs it) and the ops hardening phase; and at 15:59 the next money phase (P8b). The web defects phase is merged (15:36). Five sessions were working at once after that, more than the three I normally allow on this PC; each one checks free memory before any heavy step.
headline.baseline: Checks on main's code, run on this PC on 2026-11-14 at the merge of PR #214: backend 1435 tests (0 skipped), phone 512 tests, web 333 tests and build, all green.

phases.name: Drain tooling and fleet profile (phone app)
phases.note: Built, and passed its independent review after three passes and 25 deliberate attempts to break it: no way was found to lose, duplicate or misattribute a technician's records. The phone app also compiles natively on this PC with its changes (checked twice, the second time on the final build settings). It is finished on our side and now waits for exactly two values from you: (1) the domain name you will use (it does not have to work yet), and (2) the highest app version number on any technician's phone. It cannot merge without them, and the rest of the drain path queues behind it. Update, 2026-11-14: the reviews of the audit script (P2b-2) showed the phone has to say a little more in its record list, so this phase was reopened for a small addition (ruling C39): an identifier per phone, and a second short report after the drain of what is still on the phone and why. Its reviewer reads the addition before anything merges. It still waits for your two values. The addition is built and reviewed (2026-11-14): everything the contract asks of the phone holds. One small fix remains (ruling C46): a voice clip a technician deletes must always leave a record of that, even when the phone's storage hiccups, so the audit never mistakes a deleted clip for a lost one. Two short re-reads later (rulings C48 and C50) the code is settled: a deleted clip is described truthfully, is not uploaded, and always leaves its record. Only a wording touch-up is left, and then it waits for your two values.

phases.name: Drain audit script (backend)
phases.note: This is the script that proves the drain is complete: it compares what each phone said it held with what reached the server, record by record, and its answer is what lets you move on. Because a wrong 'all accounted for' would lose real records, it had two independent reviews, and neither let it through as it was. The first found that when two technicians share a phone, one's action could be counted as proof that the other's unsent record had arrived, with nothing printed; and that in two situations it would report a problem no action could clear. The second found that it never writes to your data, never shows a password and does run on the pinned server image, but that it read the database in many small looks instead of one, so a phone uploading in the middle could trigger a false 'stop everything'. Money records held under both: matched one to one, never written off. I set one contract for the phone side and the script side (ruling C39). The main change you will notice: after the drain, each phone sends a short second report of what is still on it and why, so the script can tell 'still uploading', 'needs entering by hand' and 'lost' apart, and every answer comes with what to do about it. Both lanes are making the changes; each goes back to its reviewer. It merges after the drain tooling (P2b-1), so it too waits for your two values. Update, 04:35 on 2026-11-14: the lane reported its fix round done, with its own tests green. I have not sent it to review yet, because it was built before four of my later rulings reached it (its turn was long and my messages waited in line). I also settled two points with it. A record that a phone gave up on without any answer from our server is not 'enter it by hand': the script will say 'tap Retry on that phone first', because a record entered by hand while the phone can still send it would end up recorded twice, and for a payment that is cash counted twice. And the option that marks the field test's records can be used for one phone at a time only, and has to list every record it marks. Update, 06:34 on 2026-11-14: the session finished the larger part (the script now reads the phone's second report, taken after the drain, and tells apart a record that is still waiting on the phone, one the technician threw away, and one that is truly lost). My three latest rulings reached it only afterwards and it is adding them now. So that no time is lost, both reviewers have started reading what is there; they run the full tests and give their verdicts when the last changes are in. Both reviewers' readings are back (06:56). Everything from the first review is fixed but one point, and they found two serious cases. In the first, a voice note that the technician discards after its job has been created would have been reported as lost for ever, stopping the whole fleet with no way to clear it. In the second, one record that arrived could be counted for two different phones, hiding a record that was really lost. Both are back with the session, with a handful of smaller ones. I also ruled that the script's one-line result must show two things it left out: payments that were discarded on a phone, with their total, so that each can be checked against what was entered by hand, and attendance records lost between the last backup and the outage. The session has answered everything (11:45 on 2026-11-14): both serious cases and all the smaller ones are fixed, each with a test, and 46 deliberate faults are each caught. The one-line result now shows discarded payments with their total and the attendance records lost before the outage. Both reviewers are on the second half: their own test runs, on today's code and on the pinned image the drain will use, then their verdicts. The session also compared the audit commands written in your runbook with what the script accepts: the two commands you will type run as written, and it found five places where the runbook's explanation falls short (for example, it never says what to do when a phone could not read one of its stores). Those go into the runbook correction that follows this merge. The first of the two verdicts is in (11:57): everything asked for is fixed, and the reviewer found one more serious case, which had been there before and comes from the way I had worded a rule. If a technician redoes an action after the phone's first report and the redone version is still waiting, or was refused, the script called the whole thing settled. It now has to judge the newer version too. A second, smaller point: a payment taken during the drain and then thrown away on the phone must appear in the one-line result. Both are back with the session; the second verdict is still to come. The second verdict is in (12:04): the full tests pass on today's code and on the pinned image the drain will use, and the reviewer could not change the result by shuffling the order of phones or reports. It found one more case of the same family as before: if one technician had the same customer-location change waiting on two phones and only one arrived, the other was called settled. That is fixed in the same round as the first reviewer's point. After that both reviewers read the changes once more. The fixes for both reviewers are in (13:35), with the full tests green again. The session pointed out one consequence of my own wording: on a phone shared by two technicians, when one redoes the other's action and it arrives, the script would have stopped the whole fleet. I corrected the rule: the phone's own report shows the replacement, so it counts as settled and both names are printed. One small change follows, then both reviewers read everything once more. That change is in (15:13), with the full tests green on both the main code and the drain code. Both reviewers are now reading everything since their last pass in one go, and one of them reruns the full tests himself. The first of the two reviewers is back (15:31): no way found for the script to call a lost write safe. One gap on the cautious side, again on a phone shared by two technicians: when the second one throws away his own refused entry after it was typed in by hand, the script stopped the whole fleet over it. I ruled that his recorded discard settles it, but only when the phone's report proves the discard came after that entry was seen. The session is building that now; the second reviewer is still running the full tests. The second reviewer passed it (15:52): he reran the full tests on both the main code and the drain code, and re-broke twelve of the script's rules one at a time to see the tests catch each. So only the one cautious-side gap from the first reviewer is left; the session is finishing that, and then both read just that last change. That last gap is closed (18:24, after the PC's stop), with the full tests green again on both the main code and the drain code. Both reviewers are reading just that change.

phases.name: Self-host repository changes
phases.note: Merged 2026-11-13 as 90ea88d after two independent review passes. It is everything the new server will run and the step-by-step runbook you will follow. The first review found four serious problems (the stand-in for the old address could answer on its own; a mistyped settings line could start the server in the wrong mode; one 'stop' step would have made every phone treat its records as refused; the restore deleted before it proved the backup). All four were fixed, and the reviewer repeated each attack and could no longer get through. Nothing is deployed: your server work (P3b) starts from this runbook once your pre-flight answers exist. The same evening its runbook section on cutting the pinned drain image was corrected in two reviewed steps (PRs #205 and #206, merged as 66e891b and 7bf9f49): it takes the timezone fix as the second of four commits, that commit is tagged so it cannot be lost, and the section now checks which commits were picked. A last correction (PR #207, merged 2026-11-14 as 53c6046) fixed the order of the final steps: the branch is pushed first, its automatic checks are read, and only then is the image tagged. Its review caught one real mistake on the way: the step for the web image would have tagged the backend commit. A larger batch of corrections to the restore, drain and backup steps (PR #209), from the rehearsal's findings, has had its first review: every correction does what it should, and the reviewer found one more gap of the same kind (a fallback path could still reach the delete step with only a damaged copy saved) and one that matters on a bad day: commands pasted through a hosting provider's emergency console could silently swallow the lines after them. Both are being fixed before it merges. Update: the batch's second review passed it with nothing left to fix (2026-11-14, at bcbf506). It merges once the rehearsal tool has typed the corrected steps end to end on its stand-in server, which is the second check I set for it. Not merged yet (06:17 on 2026-11-14): the rehearsal went through the corrected runbook with no failed step, but the tool skipped two of its steps, the one that sets the workshop's location and the one that sets the PINs, because their layout had changed. The commands in those two steps are the same as before, and the reviewer found nothing in them that could hurt your restore. I still hold the merge until the tool has run them from the corrected text: a step that was skipped was not rehearsed. The rehearsal also found one gap the correction does not close (06:21): if a restore is ever started on a server that is still running, without the first step that shuts it, nothing stops the step that deletes the database, and whatever was entered in the minutes before is lost. Today's runbook has no protection there at all, so the correction is still an improvement and is not held for this. The fix is one more check on the delete line itself, and it goes into the next runbook correction; the rehearsal tool gets a test for exactly this mistake first. The rehearsal has now tried exactly that mistake (10:38): with the first step skipped on a running server, nothing stopped the delete, in today's runbook and in the corrected one alike, and the two test entries made just before were gone. So the extra check on the delete line is needed, and it is the first item of the next runbook correction. The two skipped steps have also been run from the corrected text and pass; the merge waits only for the reviewer to repeat that run. The runbook correction (PR #209) is merged (2026-11-14, 11:32): the reviewer ran the corrected text through the rehearsal itself, every step, and confirmed it. The next correction is already under way: the check that stops a restore from deleting a database that is still in use, which the rehearsal showed to be needed. That check is written (PR #211, 12:29 on 2026-11-14): the delete step now refuses while the server is marked as in use or its program is running, and says to start again at the first step. The session tried every way into that step: the mistake now loses nothing, and every proper route (a first restore, a restore after shutting the server down, a retry after a failed load, the way back) still works. It is with its reviewer. The rehearsal tool has to be adjusted to the new text first, then it runs the new text, then this merges. Its review is back (12:52): the new check holds on every route that was tried, including the mistake it was written for, and the reviewer found one way around it. If the safety copy was taken while the server was still running, and you then cleared each warning by hand instead of going back to the first step, the delete went through and whatever was entered after the copy was lost. So the same check now also stands in front of the safety copy: no copy is accepted from a server that is still in use. Three smaller points are fixed in the same round. The reviewer read the fix (13:12): all seven points are closed and the way around the check is shut. It found one more of the same kind, which had been in the runbook all along: one line, typed on its own in a terminal that was already used for an earlier restore, could accept that earlier restore's safety copy. One small test closes it, and it is being added. The check has passed its review (13:37): the reviewer tried every way it could find to get a restore to delete data that is in no copy, and none works any more. It merges once the rehearsal tool has been adjusted to the new text and has run it. The restore correction is merged (15:54): the runbook's delete step now refuses to run on a live database, and the safety copy it relies on must have been taken in the same attempt. The rehearsal tool tried six deliberate mistakes around that step on the corrected text and each one was stopped with nothing lost.

phases.name: Web payment double-charge fix
phases.note: Merged 2026-11-13 as 15df06d, and its follow-up the same day as fa860f9, after five independent review passes in all. A payment the manager enters can no longer be recorded twice by a retry, a page reload, a second browser tab or a hung request; a slow refresh can no longer hide a payment that just landed; and a job page shows no amounts and no Log Payment button until that job's payments have actually loaded. Not deployed: it reaches the manager in the web build for the drain window.

phases.name: Web manager defects
phases.note: Started on 2026-11-14 at 13:30, on your yes. It reported ready at 14:14 (PR #212): the revenue tile now shows the week's real takings, the job board refreshes by itself every 30 seconds, error messages from the server are shown instead of swallowed, a short outage no longer signs the manager out, and a manager can record or correct a payment on a closed job with a written reason. An independent reviewer is on it since 14:15. It turned out to be needed before the drain: the web app that runs during the drain window is built with this phase in it, because during the drain the manager enters by hand whatever a phone could not send, also on jobs that are already closed, and that needs the reason field this phase adds. It also fixes the web manager's known defects (the revenue tile that shows Rs 0, the board that does not refresh, errors that are swallowed). Same files as P12a, so it builds on P12a. Deploy clause: P3c. Its review is back (14:52): all eleven fixes do what they say, and the reviewer could not break the automatic refresh or the protection against double payments. It found one thing that matters for the drain. During the drain the server is the older pinned version, which does not keep the reason a manager types for a payment on a closed job, while the form said it would. I ruled that the web then saves the reason as a note on the job by itself, and tells the manager plainly if even that fails. That and three small points are being fixed now. The fix is in (15:02): when the older server answers, the web now saves the manager's reason as a note on the job, and says plainly if even that fails. The same reviewer is checking it, and is trying to make the new step do harm (a payment sent twice, two tabs open, a lost connection between the payment and the note). The second check is back (15:13): everything from the first round is fixed and nothing else broke. The reviewer tried to make the new note-saving step do harm and found three small faults in it, none about money: two browser tabs can leave two notes for one payment; after a lost connection the note may not say which payment it is about; and if the note itself fails, the message tells the manager to add it by hand, which the web does not allow on a closed job, and the message disappears after three seconds. I ruled that all three are fixed now, in this same change, because this step exists only for the drain and is cheaper to get right once than to patch later. One more round, then the same reviewer reads it again. That round is in (15:22): one note per payment, the note names the payment only when there is no doubt which one it is, and a reason that could not be saved now stays on the job's page with a button to save it. The same reviewer is reading it again. It passed (15:31): the reviewer could not make the new step lose or misreport a reason. This PC's three checks are running on it now; when they are green it merges. Merged (15:36) after the review passed and this PC's three checks were green on the exact version. It is not deployed: it reaches the manager inside the web image that is cut for the drain. Its follow-up is up (PR #214, 15:51): a failed job creation now says why; the console no longer invents a labour rate of 1200 when it cannot read the real one; the sign-in check cannot hang for ever; and the labour rate on the Settings page is now the shop's real setting instead of demo data. A fresh reviewer is on it, looking hardest at the labour-rate editor because it changes what bills are priced with. The follow-up passed its review (16:01), and I am still holding it for one short round. The new labour-rate editor is the first screen that can change what bills are priced with. It said "Saved: Rs 1,201" when 1200.5 was typed, and a slip such as 12000 for 1200 would save at once. So before it merges: it shows exact figures, and it asks "from Rs 1,200 to Rs 12,000 per hour?" before saving anything. That round is done (18:16, after the PC's stop): the editor shows exact figures, asks before saving with both the old and the new rate, and shows what the server stored. The same reviewer is checking it. The follow-up is merged (18:29): the reviewer tried to make the labour-rate editor send a wrong value, send twice, or show one figure and save another, and could not. It reaches the manager with the deploy train, not during the drain.

phases.name: Money integrity 1: void attribution, payloads
phases.note: Merged on 2026-11-14 as 16e154e, after three independent review passes. It records who voided a payment, when and why (the first database migration of this program), makes each payment and void its own event, and builds your decision: only a manager may record or void a payment on a closed job, with a written reason. Two rules of mine came out of its reviews: text a person types is never copied into the system's event record, and a payment never fails because of a phone's clock. The last review left two small points that no app in existence can reach; they are being fixed in a short follow-up, and that follow-up must be in before the new phone app is built. Nothing changes for the shop until this is deployed; when it is, its database change is applied and checked by the steps recorded in the deploy list. The manager screens still need a small change before a manager can use the closed-job rule from the web; that goes to the web phase. Update: that follow-up (PR #210) passed its review on 2026-11-14 with nothing left to fix. It is the first thing waiting on GitHub's stopped checks: it merges as soon as they run again, or on this PC's runs if you allow that. That follow-up was merged on 2026-11-14 at 09:53, the first merge under your "yes, local checks": all three checks ran on this PC on the exact code that was merged (1435 backend tests, 512 phone tests, the web tests and build, plus the four steps GitHub runs that my local script had been missing). This phase is now complete.

phases.name: Money integrity 2: bill revisions, chain, daily check
phases.note: Proposed as a new session on 2026-11-14; it waits for your click on its card. It keeps a history of every change to a bill and extends the tamper check from staff money to customer payments. It is the first link of the chain that ends in Odoo. The small money follow-up it builds on is merged now, so it can start from the main branch. You started it on 2026-11-14 at 15:59. It keeps every version of a bill instead of overwriting it, and extends the tamper check from staff money to payments and bills. You chose email for the daily tamper-check result (18:16). The address and the mail account are typed on the server at host setup; this phase does not wait for them.

phases.note: Merged 2026-11-13 as 34f1dcd after two independent review passes. Today's app compiles to an APK on this PC (24 minutes the first time, about 75 seconds after that), and the paid location kit (version 5.8.2) compiles on SDK 52. From now on any change to the phone app's build setup is compiled here before its review can pass. A small hardening follow-up is with the same lane.

phases.name: Device lab (emulator on this PC)
phases.note: The first part (L3a) built the emulator, a local backend and a stand-in for the dead production host on this PC, and ran the first checks of today's app. Its independent review came back at 20:03. The safety question passed: no lab command can reach a real phone plugged into this PC. But four of its results did not match its own logs. The clearest: one known tracker defect was reported as not seen, while the log shows it happening three times out of three; and one check could never fail. They went back to be corrected and re-run, and no lab result is used to design the phone repair until the same reviewer has re-read them. The drain rehearsal on the emulator comes after that. The re-run was cut off when the PC shut down on the evening of 2026-11-13; the lab was restarted after the reboot and continues. Update: I paused the lab at 04:10 on 2026-11-14 and had its emulator stopped. Your own diagnosis that night showed what the freezes come from, and the emulator was the largest single thing of mine on the machine while two long test lanes were also running. It resumes when they are done, and from now on it never runs beside several test runs.

phases.name: Deploy-train and restore rehearsal
phases.note: It rehearsed, on this PC and against a stand-in database, the restore you will run by hand on the new server and the later deploy sequence, typing the runbook's own commands and trying deliberate wrong turns. Its independent review ran both rehearsals again and got the same results, confirmed its findings about the runbook, and found more. The ones that matter for you: one check would have stopped you at a perfectly good restore (and your real backup is almost certainly in exactly that state); the step that deletes and restores the database had no guard, so a failed safety backup, or simply a new terminal window, could have left you with an empty database and a restore that then fails; and one step needs a time that only the following step records. All of these go to the runbook's lane as one batch, and from now on the rehearsal can test a runbook change before it is merged, not after. The rehearsal tool itself goes back for fixes too: it must start from the pinned server image the way the real server will, so that the first database change in the deploy list is rehearsed properly. Separately it found the nightly jobs running five hours late (being fixed in the code). Update, 05:56 on 2026-11-14: the fixes are in. The tool now starts from the pinned server image, and it proves that its own checks can fail: 18 deliberate faults, one per kind of check, all caught. The first trial of that exposed one of its checks that could never have failed; it is fixed. It also rehearsed the corrected runbook before that correction is merged: the restore goes through with no failed step, where today's runbook fails at three. Two steps of the corrected runbook were not typed, because their layout changed in a way the tool refuses to guess at; that is being settled before the runbook correction merges. The second review has begun with the reading, and it will run the rehearsals itself once the session has stopped adding to them. The reading half of the second review is back (06:17): everything from the first review is fixed except one thing, and it found two serious points of its own. First, in some places the tool still picks a command by its position in a block instead of by what it says, and in one case that made it report eight safety checks as passed when it had not tried any of them. Second, two rehearsals started at the same time destroy each other and mix up their results. Both went straight back to the session, together with six smaller ones, so they are fixed in the same round. The session has finished its fix round (10:38 on 2026-11-14, after the morning's restart of the PC): both serious points and the smaller ones are answered, all 18 deliberate faults are caught again, and the corrected runbook now goes through with every step run, including the two that had been skipped. The reviewer is repeating the rehearsals itself, with ten faults of its own, before it gives its verdict. Merged on 2026-11-14 at 11:41. The reviewer repeated all the rehearsals itself and got the same result row for row, caught all 18 deliberate faults again, and confirmed that a second rehearsal started by mistake is now refused without harming the first. A short follow-up tightens four smaller points it noted. From here on, every change to the runbook is rehearsed with this tool before it is merged. Its follow-up is ready (PR #213, 14:52): the tool now reads both the current runbook and the corrected one, and it gained four more deliberate mistakes around the restore. On today's runbook each of them ends in the database being deleted; on the corrected runbook each is stopped with nothing lost. The reviewer is repeating those runs. The follow-up is merged (15:45): the reviewer repeated every run and got the same rows. With the tool on main it also rehearsed the corrected runbook, and every deliberate mistake around the restore was stopped with nothing lost. That was the condition for merging the runbook correction.

p0aDone: Done when items 1-4, 6 (every roster phone), 10 and 12 have values; the rest have values or a dated 'unknown, because ...'.

p0a.title: Tools and access
p0a.do: Start Docker Desktop. Install Android platform-tools (adb), build-tools (apksigner) and a JDK. Log in: EAS, GitHub CLI, Railway CLI (only if you control the old Railway hostname). Check you can log in to the Railway, Supabase, Cloudflare, Sentry, Firebase and Expo dashboards. Turn on USB debugging on every roster phone. Have a cable and a spare Android phone (for P2c).
p0a.why: Every other item uses these. It is done first, before item 1.
p0a.helper: tools-check.sh. adb, apksigner and a JDK are already installed for you in C:/Users/User/.fixflow-cache/android/ (nothing was added to the system PATH: the first command below loads them into one terminal)
p0a.result: e.g. docker yes, adb yes, apksigner yes, JDK yes, logins 6/6, USB debugging on 5/5 phones

p0a.title: Send the fleet hold notice
p0a.do: Edit the draft in docs/program/notices/fleet-hold.md (fill the square-bracket words), send it to every technician (English and Urdu), then replace its status line with the date, channel and who it went to, keeping the text exactly as sent.
p0a.why: Opening, updating, uninstalling or tapping Discard on a phone can lose records that never reached the server.

p0a.title: Railway first: seal the old secret, cut old services off
p0a.do: Record the Railway project state. Copy the old FIXFLOW_JWT_SECRET from the Railway environment and seal it offline (never into this page). Then remove DATABASE_URL from, or scale to 0, any surviving service, and reset the Supabase database password in its dashboard. Record whether you can bind the old subdomain (H) and to what, and your account and billing access.
p0a.why: An old backend could otherwise drain phones or run its 02:30 pruner on the old data.
p0a.result: e.g. secret sealed yes; services cut 2/2; DB password reset yes; H = yes/no

p0a.title: Archive the R2 backups
p0a.do: Mint an R2 API token (type it only into your own terminal). List backups/db/, copy it to archive/pre-selfhost/, make a laptop copy in C:/fixflow-r2, then list the archive prefix and record both listings.
p0a.why: Backups can be pruned; this keeps a copy that nothing old can delete.
p0a.helper: r2-archive.sh (set AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in your own terminal first; never paste them here or into chat)
p0a.result: e.g. 31 files listed; archive listed 31; laptop copy yes

p0a.title: Supabase: take the dump and verify it, same day
p0a.do: Record status, pause date, the restore deadline shown, Postgres major version. If restorable: restore it and take the dump now through the session pooler, sha256 it, upload it to the R2 archive, and verify it the same day with design Appendix C. If only a dashboard download exists, convert it (see the plan). If unrecoverable: screenshot. 'Unknown' is not accepted, and 'project restored' alone is not enough.
p0a.why: The real data's last copy. Its restore deadline can run out; the recovery case (a/b/c) and P9-0b depend on it.
p0a.helper: supabase-dump.sh then verify-dump.sh (set FIXFLOW_SUPABASE_URL in your own terminal first; never paste it here or into chat)
p0a.result: e.g. restorable yes; PG 15; dump sha256 first 8 chars; Appendix C passed yes

p0a.title: Fleet roster
p0a.do: For each phone: which technician id, maker / model / Android version, and whether it is shared.
p0a.why: Every later phone step (drain, install, release) is per phone.
p0a.helper: phone-facts.sh (read-only on the phone: it never opens the app; needs adb and apksigner)

p0a.title: Field build facts, per phone
p0a.do: Pull each phone's installed app (adb), read its signing certificate (apksigner), versionCode, whether the bundle contains jobs.outbox.v2 (v2) and which API host it has baked in. Compare the certificate with the EAS keystore (K). Export the keystore.
p0a.why: K, H and v2 choose which drain branch each phone takes. The keystore cannot be re-made.
p0a.helper: phone-facts.sh (read-only on the phone: it never opens the app; needs adb and apksigner)
p0a.result: per phone: K yes/no, v2 yes/no, versionCode; keystore exported yes

p0a.title: Photos of what is stuck, per phone, today
p0a.do: Airplane mode on and Wi-Fi off, open FixFlow, photograph the clock screen's DID-NOT-SYNC list and every job banner, close the app, airplane mode off. 'Not reachable' only for a phone whose login is gone.
p0a.why: The only record of what each phone still holds if a drain cannot happen.

p0a.title: Sentry
p0a.do: Backend project: date of last event. Mobile project: does it still receive events?
p0a.why: Confirms error tracking for the phones still works (decided: Sentry stays).
p0a.result: e.g. backend last event 2026-06-30; mobile ingests yes

p0a.title: Workshop location and fence size
p0a.do: The workshop's coordinates and the fence radius you want (at least 100 m).
p0a.why: P3b and P5a block without it.

p0a.title: Decisions
p0a.do: Answer every decision row (the board further down) or leave it to its default. Includes the address for the daily tamper-check email and a mail account to send it through (you chose email on 2026-11-14; both are typed on the server later, so have them ready, do not send them to me), geofence thresholds, drain host, SDK spike, shift reminder, Odoo plan and version.
p0a.why: The plan branches on these; a default is a valid answer.
p0a.helper: the decisions board on this page

p0a.title: Cut the app's network, every phone
p0a.do: In system settings, turn off FixFlow's Wi-Fi and mobile data (or background data off plus Wi-Fi blocked by a named method, or airplane mode if nothing else works). Record method and date per phone.
p0a.why: Stops a phone sending to a wrong or old server. It lifts only per the plan's branch box.

p0a.title: Restrict the committed client keys
p0a.do: In the Maps, Firebase and Sentry consoles, restrict each client key to the app's package name and SHA-1. Record done per key.
p0a.why: These keys are in the code; restriction makes them useless elsewhere.
p0a.result: e.g. Maps yes, Firebase yes, Sentry yes

p0a.title: Workshop Wi-Fi facts
p0a.do: Does the workshop have Wi-Fi the technicians' phones join during shifts? Its name (SSID), the access point id(s) (BSSID), and which phones join it. 'No Wi-Fi' is a valid answer.
p0a.why: Feeds an attendance rule; 'no Wi-Fi' simply turns that rule off.
p0a.result: e.g. yes, SSID name, 1 BSSID, phones 1-4

p0a.title: Who holds cash in the field
p0a.do: Do technicians hold cash collected at customers, or receive online payments into personal wallets, before handing them to the shop? For how long, and who counts the hand-over?
p0a.why: Decides whether the accounting needs a cash-remittance source. 'Never: every rupee reaches the manager the same day' is valid.
p0a.result: e.g. yes, up to 2 days, manager counts

p0a.title: Books basis
p0a.do: Registered for sales tax (SRB/FBR)? Books on cash basis? Is there an accountant, and do they want per-transaction entries or periodic totals? A second money writer (counter POS, offline web, second shop) planned within 12 months?
p0a.why: Shapes the Odoo hand-off. Unknowns are answered later in P9-0b, not here.
p0a.result: e.g. not registered; cash; accountant yes, weekly totals; no

machine.docker: Docker's network address pools are used up by another project (29 networks). The gate scripts work around it: they share the database container's network, and anything needing a real network uses 10.77.0.0/16. rules: No phone gets a new app until its stuck data has been drained and the after-check passed. Never uninstall, except in the one documented branch with your written sign-off per phone.
No claim that geofencing works without evidence from the fleet's own phone models.
During the drain the server runs one pinned image and nothing else.
The automatic WhatsApp dispatcher stays off until every phone is drained or retired.
The old Railway address may only hang (or, in one branch, proxy). It never answers on its own.
Technicians stay on hold until the written release notice.
Money is whole paisa; no money feed runs off the event cursor; the outbox never deletes a write.
